ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is a series resistor R, and the reference arrow of voltage U is drawn below this resistor and points left. On the right side is a bridge resistor network; the current in the upper-right branch is labeled I1, with the arrow pointing left; the current in the lower-right branch is labeled I2, with the arrow pointing right. The two branches on the right are connected to the same right node, and this right node is then connected to the bottom loop through a vertical resistor. Reasoning: Write KCL at the right node. The lower-branch current flowing into the right node is I2, and the upper-branch current flowing out of the right node is I1, so the current through the right-side vertical return branch is I2 - I1 = 1.2 mA - 0.8 mA = 0.4 mA. According to the given circuit connection, the current magnitude in the left series resistor R is the same, and the direction is taken as from left to right. By Ohm's law, the voltage drop along the current direction is I R = 0.4 mA × 50 kΩ = 20 V. Since the reference arrow of U points left, opposite to this passive voltage-drop direction from left to right, U = -20 V.
